records.title: Beyond the worm: engineering the next generation of nematode-inspired antimicrobials.
records.abstract: The global crisis of multidrug-resistant bacteria and parasitic nematodes demands new approaches to infectious disease control. Emerging evidence suggests that gastrointestinal nematodes and the host gut microbiota are inextricably linked in a complex 'holobiont'. Parasitic nematodes have evolved in microbe-rich environments for millennia, developing innate immune defenses. This evolutionary 'arms race' has produced a diverse repertoire of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) that can target bacteria and other gut microbiota. With over 5000 AMP and AMP-like domain-encoding genes identified via computational mining, the bottleneck is validation. The integration of machine learning algorithms with advanced in vitro and ex vivo models will allow prediction of AMP mode of action, spectrum of activity, and efficacy, followed by testing in organoids to address some of the limitations of animal models.

records.title: SLC9A8 deficiency impairs the integrity of the intestinal mechanical barrier by inducing endoplasmic reticulum stress.
records.abstract: SLC9A8 contributes to intestinal barrier function, but its role in mechanical barrier integrity remains unclear. To elucidate the impact of SLC9A8 deficiency on mechanical barrier integrity and the underlying mechanisms. Wild-type and Slc9a8-/- mice received 2% DSS to induce colitis. Intestinal organoids and Caco-2 cells were used for in vitro studies. Paracellular permeability, western blot, SLC9A8 siRNA, SLC9A8 inhibitor (EIPA), and ER stress (ERS) inhibitor (4-PBA) were applied. Slc9a8-/- mice showed increased susceptibility to DSS-induced colitis with worsened mucosal barrier damage and inflammatory injury. Both in vivo and in vitro, SLC9A8 deficiency impaired mechanical barrier, evidenced by increased paracellular permeability and altered tight junction protein expression. RNA-seq and bioinformatics revealed significant ERS in Slc9a8-/- mice, confirmed by elevated IRE1α, GRP78, XBP1s, ATF6, ATF4, and Chop. 4-PBA inhibition of ERS significantly decreased Claudin-2, reduced FITC-dextran flux, and restored transepithelial electrical resistance in Caco-2 monolayers. SLC9A8 maintains intestinal mechanical barrier integrity by alleviating ERS.

records.title: Temporal changes in subcellular localization of synaptic proteins in human inner ear organoids recapitulate ribbon synapse development.
records.abstract: Ribbon synapses in mechanosensitive hair cells of the inner ear are essential for transmitting mechanical stimulation to electrical signals in sensory neurons, allowing for precise and persistent neurotransmission. During hair cell development, synaptic ribbons increase in volume, while decreasing in number. Moreover, the number of synaptic vesicles tethered to ribbons increases, and synaptic proteins accumulate near the active zones. Little is known about whether ribbon synapses in organoid models recapitulate the dynamic changes in ribbon synapse development in vivo. By employing 3D high-resolution imaging, we demonstrate that CTBP2-positive presynaptic ribbons exhibit temporal changes in the number, size, and shape during hair cell maturation in human inner ear organoids. Additionally, the number of neuronal processes contacting hair cells decreases over time, suggesting projection refinement. Temporal and morphological changes are consistent with ribbon synapse maturation in mouse hair cells, suggesting equivalent ribbon assembly and refinement in human organoid hair cells.

records.title: Disruption of cell-type-specific molecular programs of striatal spiny projection neurons in autism.
records.abstract: Rare genetic variants contribute substantially to autism spectrum disorder (ASD), yet the regulatory logic of vulnerable subcortical cells is poorly understood. In a 16p11.2 deletion mouse model, lineage tracing across five brain regions revealed prominent striatal changes. In the human putamen from ASD and neurotypical donors, single-nucleus multi-omics showed transcriptional alterations concentrated in D1 striosome spiny projection neurons (SPNs), affecting synaptic and energy metabolism genes, with altered synapse-supporting programs in astrocytes. Gene regulatory network analysis integrating chromatin accessibility and expression identified EGR1 and EGR3 as key regulators of these programs, with reduced activity in D1 striosome SPNs. Deleting EGR1 or EGR3 in human striatal organoids produced partially overlapping transcriptional changes. These findings establish the striatum as a site of molecular convergence in ASD and provide a multi-omic resource for dissecting subcortical mechanisms.

records.title: A patient-derived, autologous component-integrated biomimetic hydrogel system for lung cancer organoid culture and recapitulation of immunotherapy response.
records.abstract: Matrigel-based culture of patient-derived lung cancer organoids (LCOs) is limited by undefined composition, batch-to-batch variability, and immunogenicity, which compromise experimental reproducibility and drug response readouts. We developed an autologous component-integrated hydrogel by incorporating patient-derived decellularized lung fiber fragments (1.25 μm diameter; 52.5 μm length) and optimized autologous plasma (56 °C, 30 min; 8,000×g, 5 min; 5% v/v) into a porous gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) network. Five formulations-GelMA, GelMA+ fiber, GelMA + plasma, MC-GelMA (fibers + plasma) and Matrigel-were compared to dissect component contributions. LCOs were established from 8 patients, and PBMC co-culture experiments were performed with 3 samples (1 PD-L1-positive, 2 PD-L1-negative). MC-GelMA exhibited uniform porosity and a Young's modulus of 15.67 ± 0.86 kPa, closely matching native lung tumor tissue. Compared with Matrigel, LCOs cultured in MC-GelMA exhibited in vivo-like morphology, enhanced viability and metabolic activity, and preservation of key histological and genomic features.The platform supported stable long-term culture through passage 9 with maintained drug sensitivity. Component analysis revealed that fibers mainly provided structural and mechanical cues, while plasma supplied biochemical signals; their combination synergistically enhanced organoid growth and immune cell infiltration. In co-culture, MC-GelMA recapitulated anti-PD-L1 responses: PD-L1-positive organoids showed increased LDH release, whereas PD-L1-negative organoids did not respond. In conclusion, this autologous component-integrated biomimetic hydrogel serves as a highly reproducible biofabrication platform for stable LCO culture and reliable recapitulation of patient-specific immunotherapy response patterns. Further validation in larger cohorts is warranted to establish its predictive potential for clinical immunotherapy outcomes.

records.title: Virtual metrology for process perturbation prediction in lithographic alignment marks using a physics-guided directed attention network.
records.abstract: Process perturbations in lithographic alignment marks deform multilayer profiles, break mark symmetry, and introduce alignment position uncertainty. Although alignment position deviation (APD) and wafer quality (WQ) responses contain process-dependent information, retrieving the underlying perturbations remains challenging because the inverse relationship is nonlinear and strongly coupled. We formulate this task as alignment mark virtual metrology, in which process perturbation values are estimated from paired APD/WQ response matrices. To solve this inverse problem, we propose a physics-guided directed attention network (PG-DAN). PG-DAN uses diffraction limit masked attention (DLMA) to inject wavelength, diffraction order, propagation, locality, and identity priors into APD/WQ attention logits, enabling the model to use physically meaningful token relations rather than unconstrained data correlations. A directed decoder further follows multilayer coupling during prediction. Evaluated on a rigorous coupled wave analysis (RCWA) dataset, PG-DAN achieves a mean R2 of 0.999875, a mean range-normalized RMSE of 0.34%, and a mean range-normalized MAE of 0.23%, with lower estimation errors than conventional neural inverse models. These results support physics-guided inverse modeling for alignment mark process perturbation estimation.

records.title: Single-cell perturbation prediction near experimental reproducibility with GENESIS.
records.abstract: Single-cell perturbation atlases now measure cellular responses across millions of cells, but the number of possible combinations of biological contexts, perturbations, doses and other experimental variables make exhaustive measurements infeasible. Here, we present GENESIS (Generative ENErgy-based Single-cell Intervention Simulator), a generative framework that predicts single-cell response distributions directly from the covariates defining an experimental condition. GENESIS uses a lightweight neural network trained with the energy score, a strictly proper scoring rule for distributions. We introduce an experiment-calibrated evaluation framework in which prediction error is interpreted relative to the reproducibility of repeated measurements of the same condition. Across the Tahoe-100M small-molecule atlas and a large PBMC cytokine atlas, GENESIS significantly outperforms existing generative models and statistical baselines and approaches experimental reproducibility on independently repeated conditions. Importantly, GENESIS remains accurate when trained on only a fraction of the available experimental conditions or cells, and generated profiles recover experimentally observed context-dependent transcriptional programs. At comparable training-cell budgets, GENESIS achieves more accurate predictions when measurements span more experimental conditions rather than profiling fewer conditions more deeply. Together, these findings suggest a complementary strategy for perturbation studies: broader, lower-depth measurements can expand experimental coverage, while GENESIS augments sparsely sampled populations and predicts responses in unmeasured conditions.

records.title: MultiFlow: coupled flow matching for predicting single-cell multiomic perturbation responses in unseen cellular contexts.
records.abstract: Predicting cellular responses to perturbation requires resolving coordinated changes across molecular layers, yet most single-cell perturbation models focus on transcriptional responses alone. Here we present MultiFlow, a coupled flow-matching framework that unifies generation and perturbation prediction of paired gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Through bidirectional information exchange between RNA and ATAC generative flows, MultiFlow learns how their joint distribution depends on cellular context and perturbation identity. Across multiomic generation benchmarks, MultiFlow accurately reproduced paired RNA-ATAC states and their population distributions. In multiome perturbation benchmarks, MultiFlow achieved the strongest overall performance in predicting both gene-expression and chromatin-accessibility perturbation responses, outperforming modality-specific perturbation-prediction methods in cell types whose perturbed states were withheld from training. Joint multiomic modeling further preserved perturbation-induced coordination between modalities, including concordant peak-gene effects and cross-modal cellular neighborhood structure. These results establish MultiFlow as a unified generative framework for modeling paired molecular states and predicting their coordinated perturbation responses across cellular contexts. Code and tutorial of MultiFlow are available at https://github.com/liuq-lab/MultiFlow.

records.title: Prediction transfer does not imply reliability transfer in single-cell foundation models.
records.abstract: Single-cell foundation models are increasingly transferred across tissues, diseases, perturbation screens, and experimental platforms. Although substantial effort has focused on prediction transfer, it remains unclear whether a model's assessment of its own reliability transfers similarly across biological contexts. Here we define reliability transfer as the ability to transfer an accurate assessment of when model predictions are likely to be correct or incorrect and investigate its behavior across ten perturbation-prediction systems spanning multiple datasets, models, and evaluation settings. We find that reliability transfer varies substantially across source-target pairs and cannot be inferred from predictive performance alone, indicating that prediction transfer and reliability transfer constitute distinct forms of generalization. Analyses of biological annotations, network connectivity, target exposure, and contextual factors reveal that prediction reliability is associated with both shared and context-dependent signals, with their relative importance differing across systems. To characterize this variability, we introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints, context-level signatures derived from strictly cross-fitted SHAP explanations that summarize how reliability estimators combine biological and contextual information when assigning confidence. Across systems, contexts with similar attribution-magnitude fingerprints tended to transfer reliability more successfully, and fingerprint similarity identified transfer sources achieving higher reliability-transfer performance within the observed candidate set. However, these relationships weakened under stricter cross-family transfer settings, indicating that transferable reliability structure remains partly dependent on shared contextual information. Finally, transferred reliability estimators produced different perturbation rankings despite identical perturbation predictions, illustrating a practical consequence of reliability transfer for downstream prioritization. Together, these results establish reliability transfer as a distinct aspect of foundation-model generalization and introduce reliability-attribution fingerprints as a framework for characterizing transferable reliability structure across biological contexts.

records.title: Artificial Cells and Biomimetic Cells: Intelligent Systems Driving a Paradigm Shift in Drug Discovery and Delivery.
records.abstract: The convergence of synthetic biology, materials science, and artificial intelligence drives a transformative shift in biopharmaceutical research, advancing from passive drug carriers to intelligent, programmable therapeutics. This review evaluates artificial and biomimetic cells as a framework that connects fundamental biological discovery with clinical translation. It examines five key technological pathways: membrane-engineered artificial cells, membraneless organelle (MLO) systems, multicompartmental artificial cells, protocell communication networks, and virtual cells. These platforms enable precise regulation of drug stability, targeting, biosynthesis, and adaptive responsiveness. Recent progress includes microenvironment-triggered release, logic-gated intercellular communication, and virtual cell-assisted high-throughput screening and toxicity prediction. Despite these advances, challenges remain in scalable manufacturing, long-term stability, and regulatory adaptation. The integration of closed-loop learning, interpretable models, and advanced biomanufacturing will be essential to position artificial and biomimetic cell systems at the forefront of next-generation precision medicine.

records.title: The Tenocyte from Atom to Cell: A Critical Multiscale Synthesis Linking Collagen Chemistry, Tissue Mechanics, Cell Mechanobiology and Mathematical Modelling.
records.abstract: The tenocyte builds, maintains, senses and degrades one of the most mechanically demanding extracellular matrices in vertebrates, yet the chemical, physical, biological and mathematical descriptions of this system have developed in largely separate literatures. This review examines the tenocyte-matrix unit as a single causal system spanning eight orders of magnitude in length, organised around five transitions: from collagen chemistry to molecular mechanics; from molecule to fibril and fascicle; from tissue loading to the cellular mechanical stimulus; from stimulus to transcription; and from cellular output back to matrix composition. At each transition, we weigh competing hypotheses, identify where evidence is decisive and where it remains correlative, and state the governing equations. We integrate advances from 2021-2026, including single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlases of human tendons, the establishment of PIEZO1 as a causal regulator of tendon stiffness, and microstructurally derived constitutive models. We argue that tendon homeostasis is a closed-loop control problem, formalised as a mechanostat with an inverted-U dose-response, and that the recurrent pathologies of tendon-tendinopathy, ageing, diabetic stiffening and fibrotic healing are failures of this loop rather than of any single component. An open-source computational companion (tenocyte-virtual-cell) is introduced, and a prioritised research agenda closes the review.

records.title: Protein engineering in Brazil: a biophysical perspective.
records.abstract: Protein engineering has become an increasingly interdisciplinary field, integrating molecular biology, structural biology, biophysics, computational modeling, and artificial intelligence to modify protein structure, stability, dynamics, molecular recognition, and catalytic activity. This systematic review examines the historical development and scientific contributions of protein engineering research associated with Brazilian institutions between 1988 and June 2026. A total of 792 peer-reviewed articles were identified in PubMed through eight thematic search strategies covering protein and enzyme engineering, directed evolution, rational and computational design, recombinant protein expression, therapeutic proteins, structural biology, and artificial intelligence-assisted engineering. The reviewed literature reveals a transition from early residue-level mutagenesis and conventional biochemical assays to increasingly integrated experimental and computational approaches. Advances in X-ray crystallography, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), circular dichroism (CD), mass spectrometry, small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), calorimetry, molecular dynamics, and structural bioinformatics enabled the quantitative investigation of protein folding, stability, conformational landscapes, molecular interactions, and catalytic mechanisms. More recently, machine learning, protein language models, AlphaFold-derived structures, and generative approaches have expanded the capacity to predict mutations and design proteins, peptides, antibodies, and enzymes with predefined properties. Overall, protein engineering in Brazil has evolved into a mature and diverse field with applications in health, infectious diseases, agriculture, biotechnology, bioenergy, biomaterials, environmental remediation, and industrial biocatalysis. The findings indicate that biophysics has moved beyond a predominantly descriptive role and has become central to the design and validation of engineered proteins. Future progress will depend on the convergence of experimental biophysics, multiscale simulations, artificial intelligence, high-throughput validation, and stronger national and international research networks.

records.title: Evolutionary divergence of uric acid catabolic enzymes: structure-function constraints and genomic innovations across taxa.
records.abstract: Uric acid degradation is a model for understanding how gene duplication, loss, and functional divergence drive metabolic evolution. In hominoids and uricotelic animals, uric acid is the terminal purine catabolite, whereas most other taxa further degrade it to allantoin and beyond. Comparative genomics and structural analyses reveal recurrent duplication and repurposing of key enzymes. 5-Hydroxyisourate hydrolase (HIUase) and transthyretin (TTR) share a common ancestral hydrolase, later diverging through neofunctionalization, while independent gene fusions reshaped the pathway, notably the gene fusion of Urah (HIUase) and Urad (2-oxo-4-hydroxy-4-carboxy-5-ureidoimidazoline decarboxylase, or OHCUd) into single-chain allantoin synthases in plants, diatoms, and bacteria. Elastic network modeling this gene fusion shows uncorrelated motions between the catalytic domains, suggesting its advantage stems from fixed stoichiometry and spatial proximity rather than conformational coupling. Further divergence is seen in enzyme families with complementary substrate specificities, and gene clustering in bacteria and yeast reflects regulatory optimization under nitrogen limitation, paralleling the ureide pathway in legumes. In hominoids, pseudogenization of urate oxidase relaxed constraints on downstream enzymes, elevating serum uric acid, an ancestral adaptation now linked to hyperuricemia. Gut microbiome-mediated degradation and links between Urad variants and cancer risk underscore the pathway's continuing relevance. Mammalian Urad orthologs show strong sequence conservation. Molecular modeling of the human ortholog demonstrated a conserved fold, consistent with a predominantly α-helical secondary structure content supported by circular dichroism, whereas kinetic characterization revealed the absence of detectable catalytic activity. Building on these principles, evolution-guided protein engineering achieved partial functional interconversion between transthyretins and HIUases without disrupting the ancestral scaffold, revealing purine catabolism's plasticity as a model for enzyme innovation and the metabolism-disease-protein design interface.

records.title: PFM: perturbed flow matching for structure-based drug design.
records.abstract: Target-specific 3D molecular generation is a promising approach for structure-based drug design. However, existing diffusion-based methods are generally restricted to marginal distributions with closed-form solutions, limiting the flexibility of generative process design, especially for the forward noising process. As a result, these methods may be less effective in modeling the complex distributions underlying pocket-conditioned molecular generation. We develop Perturbed Flow Matching (PFM), a flow-matching-based framework for protein pocket-conditioned 3D molecular generation. PFM employs a perturbed conditional probability path that incorporates both pocket binding-site information and coupled atom type-coordinate information, enabling more effective generation of molecules in protein binding environments. On CrossDocked2020, PFM achieves competitive structural quality and the best average Vina score among the evaluated unguided methods (-7.12); PFM-G further improves the score to -8.70 with tailored classifier-free guidance. Experiments on additional molecular datasets further confirm the effectiveness and generalizability of the proposed framework. https://github.com/kurisu92725/PFM.

records.title: De novo design of miniprotein inhibitors of bacterial adhesins.
records.abstract: The rise of multidrug-resistant bacterial infections necessitates the discovery of novel antimicrobial strategies. Here, we show that protein design provides a generalizable means of generating new antimicrobials by neutralizing the function of bacterial adhesins, which are virulence factors critical in host-pathogen interactions. We de novo designed high-affinity miniprotein binders to FimH and Abp chaperone usher pili adhesins from uropathogenic Escherichia coli and Acinetobacter baumannii, respectively, which are implicated in mediating both uncomplicated and catheter-associated urinary tract infections (UTI) responsible for significant morbidity worldwide. The designed antagonists have high specificity and stability, disrupt bacterial recognition of host receptors, block biofilm formation, and are effective in treating and preventing murine models of uncomplicated and catheter-associated UTIs in vivo.

records.title: Pharmacophore-Conditioned Diffusion Model for Ligand-Based De Novo Drug Design.
records.abstract: Developing bioactive molecules remains a central, time- and cost-heavy challenge in drug discovery, particularly for novel targets lacking structural or functional data. Pharmacophore modeling presents an alternative for capturing the key features required for molecular bioactivity against a biological target. In this work, we present PharmaDiff, a pharmacophore-conditioned diffusion model for 3D molecular generation. PharmaDiff employs a transformer-based architecture to integrate an atom-based representation of the 3D pharmacophore into the generative process, enabling the precise generation of 3D molecular graphs that align with predefined pharmacophore hypotheses. Through comprehensive testing, PharmaDiff demonstrates superior performance in matching 3D pharmacophore constraints compared to ligand-based drug design methods. Additionally, it achieves higher docking scores across a range of proteins in structure-based drug design, without the need for target protein structures. By integrating pharmacophore modeling with 3D generative techniques, PharmaDiff offers a powerful and flexible framework for rational drug design.

records.title: Programming Targeted Immune Cell Migration Using Orthogonal Chemokine-Receptor Pairs.
records.abstract: Chemokines orchestrate the migration of immune cells throughout the body, but harnessing chemokine signaling to engineer targeted cell trafficking is challenging because of their overlapping interactions and broad expression patterns. Here we used structure-guided protein design to engineer orthogonal chemokine-receptor pairs with minimal crosstalk to native systems. T cells engineered with an ortho-receptor selectively infiltrated tissues producing the ortho-chemokine, in vitro and in vivo. By engineering T cells that both sense and secrete the ortho-chemokine, we generated collective swarming behavior in which pioneer cells attract follower cells via an ortho-chemokine gradient self-organized by positive feedback. By providing orthogonal genetic control over both the generation and sensing of chemokine gradients, this system enables the construction of autonomous spatial targeting programs in engineered cells.

records.title: Deploying liquid intelligence in cancer: Finding answers in our blood.
records.abstract: Liquid biopsies are one of the few noninvasive procedures for probing disease at the molecular level. They represent a scalable solution to cancer detection and monitoring by capturing tumor-derived signals from circulating biomolecules such as proteins, DNA, RNA, and metabolites. However, these signals are often sparse, heterogeneous, and shaped by genetics, demographics, and comorbidities. Recent advances in artificial intelligence, especially with multimodal foundation models, have proven capable of extracting signals from noisy, high-dimensional data. Pretraining on large cohorts and integrating complementary modalities may improve sensitivity for tumor signals in blood, though significant clinical and infrastructural barriers remain. This review synthesizes advances in liquid biopsy technologies and artificial intelligence and examines how their convergence can enable enhanced cancer monitoring.

records.title: Plasma ATR-FTIR spectroscopy combined with machine learning for early classification of response to neoadjuvant endocrine therapy: exploratory results from the ANNE trial.
records.abstract: Neoadjuvant endocrine therapy (NET) is an effective treatment strategy for luminal breast cancer, but early identification of responders remains challenging. ATR-FTIR spectroscopy combined with machine learning may provide a low-cost, minimally invasive liquid biopsy approach for capturing biochemical information from plasma. This exploratory study was embedded within the ANNE trial, a prospective single-arm phase II study evaluating neoadjuvant anastrozole in stage II-III luminal breast cancer. Plasma ATR-FTIR spectra obtained at baseline and after 2-4 weeks of treatment were used to classify response defined by rebiopsy Ki67 and surgical PEPI, respectively. Eight classifier families, including PCA followed by linear discriminant analysis and ridge logistic regression, were evaluated in R. Hyperparameters and the use and configuration of synthetic minority oversampling (SMOTE) were selected jointly using stratified four-fold validation within an outer leave-one-out cross-validation procedure. The Ki67 analysis included 49 patients (41 responders; 8 non-responders), and the PEPI analysis included 36 patients (10 responders; 26 non-responders). The highest observed classifier-specific AUCs were 0.738 for baseline Ki67 classification using an RBF support vector machine and 0.869 for PEPI classification using k-nearest neighbors. The respective accuracies were 0.816 and 0.833, sensitivities were 0.854 and 0.800, specificities were 0.625 and 0.846, and Matthews correlation coefficients were 0.424 and 0.614. Complementary analyses showed that mandatory SMOTE did not improve every classifier. When classifier family was also selected within inner validation, AUCs were 0.616 for Ki67 and 0.854 for PEPI. Spectral features were tentatively associated with lipid-, protein-, nucleic acid- and carbohydrate-related vibrational modes. Plasma ATR-FTIR spectroscopy combined with machine learning showed exploratory potential for classifying endocrine response, with stronger observed discrimination for PEPI using on-treatment plasma than for Ki67 using baseline plasma. Joint tuning of hyperparameters and balance strategy allowed class-specific performance to be assessed without imposing oversampling on every model. The findings require external validation in larger cohorts before clinical application.

records.title: APOBEC3-mediated therapy resistance and immunogenicity in solid tumors: from genomic scars to therapeutic vulnerabilities.
records.abstract: The APOBEC3 family of cytidine deaminases, originally evolved for antiviral defense, functions as a potent source of somatic mutations in human malignancies. Although the genomic footprints of APOBEC3 were deciphered over a decade ago with characteristic mutational signatures (single-base substitution [SBS]2 and SBS13), their clinical significance is only now becoming apparent, shifting from a descriptive hallmark of mutagenesis to a potential predictor of therapy outcomes. Emerging evidence from landmark studies reveals that apolipoprotein B mRNA editing enzyme, catalytic polypeptide-like (APOBEC)-associated mutational signatures are associated with acquired resistance to targeted therapies and are an emerging biomarker of response to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Mechanistically, therapy-induced activation of APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B drives the evolution of drug-tolerant persister cells and generates genomic diversity from which resistant clones emerge-a phenomenon demonstrated across epidermal growth factor receptor inhibitor resistance in lung cancer, endocrine therapy resistance in breast cancer, and androgen receptor blockade resistance in prostate cancer. Concurrently, studies have shown that APOBEC mutational signatures are associated with ICI benefit, including in tumor mutational burden-adjusted analyses, most notably in urothelial carcinoma and non-small-cell lung cancer. In this study, we review this emerging paradigm, focusing on the newly established mechanisms and clinical findings. We further address the translational hurdles of detecting APOBEC mutational signatures in clinical practice and emerging therapeutic strategies, including oligonucleotide-based inhibitors and synthetic lethality. Finally, we discuss standardizing APOBEC mutational signature detection for clinical use, including developing liquid biopsy-based dynamic monitoring, and designing prospective trials with APOBEC mutational signature-based stratification.

records.title: PathInteract: a video analysis suite for capturing and analyzing pathology slide reviewing interactions.
records.abstract: Digital pathology has transformed how pathologists review and interpret tissue specimens, enabling remote access, efficient storage, and advanced visualization. Systematically analyzing pathologists' slide reviewing interactions can uncover opportunities to design AI-assisted tools that integrate seamlessly into routine practice. We present a proof-of-concept suite, PathInteract, for extracting pathology interaction signals from recorded slide-review videos. Mouse cursor movements, viewport actions (i.e., zooming and panning), and verbal narratives are extracted using multiple deep learning and computer vision moduals. Unlike prior methods requiring specialized software or equipment, our approach operates on screen recordings, enabling broader applicability. We developed PathInteract using QuPath-recorded diagnostic sessions with view-tracking logs and applied it to ten educational YouTube videos. Results revealed distinct interaction patterns between two pathologists with different levels of experience, tissue type, and use context. Cursor tracking and viewport detection achieved strong agreement with ground truth, while speech analysis highlighted differences in cell-level focus across diseases. PathInteract enables scalable analysis of reviewing interactions in digital pathology through video recording and supports repurposing of existing pathology videos towards building interpretable, multimodal pathology AI datasets. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-61758-2.

records.title: A noninvasive risk stratification prediction model for neuroblastoma through integration of multidimensional clinical indicators.
records.abstract: Current neuroblastoma (NB) risk classification relies partly on tumor tissue-derived information, which may be unavailable in patients who cannot undergo biopsy or surgical resection. Therefore, this study aimed to develop a non-invasive prediction model for NB risk classification by integrating a liquid biopsy biomarker with routinely available clinical indicators. A total of 141 treatment-naïve patients with NB were included and divided into a training cohort (n = 100) and a held-out testing cohort (n = 41). Six pretreatment predictors, including age, sex, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), neuron-specific enolase (NSE), image-defined risk factors (IDRFs), and circulating plasma MYCN amplification status, were incorporated into 11 machine-learning algorithms. Model development and selection were performed exclusively in the training cohort using repeated nested cross-validation with patient-level out-of-fold predictions. Random forest (RF) achieved the best overall performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.952 (95% CI, 0.906-0.998), an accuracy of 91%, and a Brier score of 0.079. Decision curve analysis showed positive net benefit across the prespecified threshold range of 15%-50%, while SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis identified IDRFs, NSE, and LDH as the leading contributors to model predictions. After model locking, the RF model retained good discrimination in the held-out testing cohort, with an AUC of 0.890 (95% CI, 0.791-0.989), a sensitivity of 84.2%, and a Brier score of 0.140. These findings support the feasibility of combining circulating MYCN status with routine clinical variables to provide a non-tissue-based approach for assisting NB risk classification. • Current NB risk classification incorporates clinical, imaging, histopathological, and molecular information, some of which requires tumor tissue and may be unavailable before biopsy or surgery. • This study developed and independently tested a non-invasive machine-learning model integrating circulating plasma MYCN amplification status with five routinely available clinical indicators, achieving an AUC of 0.952 during nested cross-validation in the training cohort and an AUC of 0.890 in the held-out testing cohort.

records.title: Recent Advancements in Diagnosis and Targeted Therapy of Pancreatic Cancer.
records.abstract: Pancreatic Cancer (PC) is an exceptionally belligerent and lethal malignancy owing to failure in prognosis and limited existing therapies. Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC) mostly originates from ductal cells, with a survival rate of less than 5 years. This cancer is predominantly caused by genetic abnormalities in the exocrine pancreas, such as KRAS and p53, which contribute to tumor growth and progression. Our previously published article on PC taught us that there is an utmost need to identify novel biomarkers for diagnosis and targeted therapy approaches to improve survival rates in patients. Conventional radiotherapy and nanotechnology-based approaches show limited success compared to targeted therapy. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Science Direct, Scopus, Bentham Science, Google Scholar, ACS Journals, and Taylor and Francis journals and Web of Science databases using keywords related to Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC), biomarkers, and targeted therapies. Articles published in English over the past two decades were screened, and studies focusing on novel biomarkers and therapeutic strategies were included for this review. Recent innovations in PDAC treatment include novel biomarkers (genetic markers, proteomic biomarkers, metabolism-related biomarkers, epigenetic markers, liquid biopsy, Pancreatic Cancer Stem Cell (PSCC) biomarkers, circulating biomarkers, and tissue biomarkers) that facilitate early diagnosis and thus minimize mortality rates. The current review highlighted the utmost need for novel targeted approaches (targeting DNA repairing and Microsatellite instability, targeting epigenetic alteration, targeting key Signaling pathways, targeting the stroma, Fibrosis, and extracellular matrix, and drug conjugate inhibitors) that enhance the specificity and efficacy against cancer cells, reduce the injury to healthy tissue, and improve survival rates. Targeted therapy also focuses on the specific molecular characteristics of cancer cells, providing a possible alternative to traditional therapies. To summarize, the shifting landscape of cancer treatment, particularly for PC, requires further study of targeted innovative combination therapies to improve patient survival while addressing the major limitations of traditional treatments. Several such products are in clinical trials, which have benefited patients with new hope suffering from PDAC.
